Only the levelized production costs carry money values: Table 4 '(US$ 2008/GJ)' and summary 'Production Costs (US$2008)'; Fig. 4 is US$2000/bbl. All are in the _production-costs sidecar; the main file has no money values.

Main file: four Canadian oil-sands technologies, text values only (the brief has no technology table). SAGD (well_sagd): description, status, steam-to-oil ratio 3.2 and natural gas 1-1.25 GJ/bbl as flows (gas converted to per m3 bitumen). CSS (well_cyclic-steam): description, status, SOR 3.4 - the brief writes 'CCS' for cyclic steam stimulation throughout, NOT carbon capture. Surface mining with hot-water extraction (separator_warm-water-extraction): description, status, oil sand >= 2 t/bbl as a flow. Bitumen upgrading (reactor_integrated-upgrader): description and status only - no per-unit data. All figures are second-hand (Alberta fact sheet 2006, NRCan GHGenius 2008, CRS 2008). Sidecars (not loaded): _emissions (Table 3 and Charpentier pathway ranges - route not split or two archetypes combined; life-cycle figures), _production-costs (Table 4, levelized), _context (recoveries, water use with unclear route, energy shares, Canadian totals, SOR target). Omitted: resource and reserve tables (Tables 1-2), tight gas, CBM, shale gas and hydrate production methods (no in-scope numbers), Figs. 5-6 projections.

(1) 'CCS' is used for cyclic steam stimulation (CSS) throughout the oil-sand text, and CSS is misnamed 'Cycle Steam Simulator' (p.2, p.3). (2) Summary Table 5 gives oil shale emissions 13.0-15.0 gCO2eq/MJ; Table 3 and the Highlights give 13-50. (3) Conventional oil '4.4 and 4.7 gCO2/MJ (27 and 58 kgCO2/bbl)': 58 kg/bbl is about 9.5 g/MJ. (4) Oil-sand reserves 246 BBL (Table 1, summary) vs 256 BBL (p.2 text). (5) p.3 text: 'CBM with 180 tcm and tight gas with 210 bcm' - 180 is the easily accessible CBM figure (total 256) and tight gas is 210 tcm. (6) Emission units switch between gCO2/MJ (Table 3) and gCO2eq/MJ (summary). (7) Decimal commas mixed with points ('19,7', '$3,8'). (8) Table 1: merged cells put the Nat.
